title: The Seder curriculum: from first source to independent study
principle: This is one integrated journey. Gemara supplies the central reading-and-reasoning spine; Torah, prayer, halakha, thought, ethics, and history provide the other source worlds in which that literacy becomes real.

levels.title: Enter the page
levels.promise: Orient to Hebrew and identify what kind of source is in front of you.

milestones.title: Read the page as a source
milestones.capability: Identify a source voice, question signal, and cited text before translating every word.

milestones.title: Map a first sugya
milestones.capability: Separate a Mishnah case from the Gemara question and a source-based response.

levels.title: Build source fluency
levels.promise: Use recurring language and source forms across more than one field of Jewish learning.

milestones.title: Recognize the recurring signals
milestones.capability: Predict whether a line is asking, citing, distinguishing, or responding before using English to check.

milestones.title: Read Torah and prayer as sources
milestones.capability: Name address, claim, command, and response in Torah and liturgical passages.

levels.title: Read an argument
levels.promise: Follow the moves that make a sugya into an argument rather than a vocabulary list.

milestones.title: Map case, distinction, and response
milestones.capability: Keep people, objects, boundaries, categories, and responses distinct in a legal source.

milestones.title: Follow question, proof, and answer
milestones.capability: Explain the pressure created by a question and the precise work a proof text or response performs.

levels.title: Read the canon in conversation
levels.promise: See how law, prayer, thought, ethics, and history ask different questions with shared discipline.

milestones.title: Trace source and reception
milestones.capability: Follow a Torah source into later practice while distinguishing study from personal halakhic guidance.

milestones.title: Hold claim and context together
milestones.capability: Identify a conceptual claim or historical setting before treating a source as an answer to everything.

levels.title: Synthesize without flattening
levels.promise: Compare sources responsibly, preserve difference, and state a real point of connection.

milestones.title: Compare interpretations
milestones.capability: Give two readings their strongest form, name their difference, and make one bounded connection.

milestones.title: Transfer a reading habit
milestones.capability: Recognize a learned move in a contrasting or unfamiliar source rather than only in its original lesson.

levels.title: Study independently
levels.promise: Enter an unfamiliar page, create a defensible first map, and know what to do with uncertainty.

milestones.title: Read an unfamiliar sugya
milestones.capability: Map a short unknown sugya, use translation to verify, and state one question worth pursuing.

milestones.title: Choose a responsible next step
milestones.capability: Use retrieval, a source map, vocabulary support, and appropriate human resources without pretending uncertainty is mastery.
